reviews.text: Unfortunately there is just not enough game here. Within practically one hour I easily feel like I've seen everything this game has to offer. These types of games live and die by the ability to provide different builds and upgrade paths to experiment and play with, and this game just doesn't have even close to the quantity required to make this a highly re-playable experience. The only real difference run to run is what order you get the few upgrades they do have handed to you. I know it's new and in early access but it really should have had some extra time in the oven. It's a shame too because the visuals and sound design are incredibly well done, but I guess this means that they have a super solid core to work with. Maybe I'll repurchase if they manage to add an adequate amount of variety to make different runs feel interesting and unique, but for now it just doesn't have enough here.

I picked this game up because NOVA DRIFT released a steam announcement down the line and was like "Oh yeah there's this game that I like called UTOPIA MUST FALL you should check it out or something idk" (not the exact words), and yeah. I was hooked. Immediately. I feel like this game was made for me. It's a kind of game I *like* and I can't explain why. Anyway, it's not a long game, nor do you make progress between runs. it is a Roguelike. Most runs don't last long, and I'm enjoying it as a timewaster. Sometimes it's nice to just have a game I boot up and play for a bit when I don't know what to do. It's a pretty neat looking game. Surprisingly, everything feels rather clear. I kinda know what everything is going to do at a glance, once I've seen an enemy before. There's like, three "Playstyles"? Three major upgrade routes, two of those are secret. You'll figure it out, I'm sure (check the challenge guide if you want it spelt out), I don't think there's an upgrade that feels useless either? It's all pretty good, there's just things you need NOW and things you can have LATER. Keep in mind, there's no winning as far as I must know. My longest run so far is about day 36, sitting at around 861,641 score. I ran down to my final 9 tactical missiles, and then that bastard Purple Nullifier Rift That I Hate appeared and single handedly handicapped me so hard it killed the run. I nod, knowing it was a good run. This part of the 'review' is the nerd ♥♥♥♥ I like to do. It's not a needed read, since all you really need to know is "Short, fun, it wasn't designed for you to win. Utopia Must Fall. Nice sound design, nice music that's fitting. Nice aesthetics. Do you like a good time waster and wanna kill some time now and then? You can do a lot worse. That being said, there's a few things that could do with some tweaking. Some enemy squadrons immediately kill runs based on build or RNG, those little spinny projectiles that cna't be destroyed with coilgun rounds? Hate those things, though I understand their purpose, without nuclear missiles you're locked with some randomness whether or not you can deal with them. Most of my runs die because of those things. Still a good game though." But! if you do like nerd ♥♥♥♥, and enjoy people thinking waaaay too deep about games, I hope you enjoy! My FAVOURITE thing about this game? It's the tone. I was expecting some arcady music, something high octane or something. What I got was... Actually a very quiet soundtrack, and a game that, in my opinion, does a fantastic job at conveying scale and desperation with so little. It starts, showing you a landmark you'll recognise, and the name of a city. Then it zooms out, you see vehicles flying around in the sky, floating past said landmark, then you see the structures in the background. Structures that dwarf the landmarks we know so well. ANd then structures that dwarf *those* structures. And then you see the cannon. The cannon looks, small, compared to the city. I wonder how big it must be compared to your average person. Or, hell, the landmark in the city. It makes a constant, distant echo as it fires. You land a few coil-rounds in a hostile ship passing by, a faint explosion. Currently, the gun is only firing about 600 RPM. The first waves aren't too bad, just a few asteroid chunks here and there. Some formation fighters. A centipede or two. You survive the first day, "APOCALYPSE AVERTED!" the game informs you. You get your first upgrade, buying EMERGENCY STOCKPILE - three nuclear warheads from an international arms market. The screen zooms out a little. More invaders show up. The days keep passing. You get multiple upgrades from performing well. Your coilgun fires an extra 300, 600, more rounds. Maybe your shield fires off extremely dangerous electric arcs at nearby enemies or hostile projectiles. Perhaps your city is producing one nuke every 2 days. Or one every day, maybe two. Maybe you have a watch tower or two sitting outside the city, providing covering fire to keep the city safe. The first week passes. The screen has zoomed out a lot by now. You go to buy a stockpile, you can't. The option is greyed out. "Unavailable. The International Arms Markets have been destroyed." That's when my favourite track plays, "Re-Evaluate Your Priorities." How many cities are still standing, I wonder? Is this the only one thats left? I mentioned the distant, echoing sounds of the coil-cannon. Your second week, by now it's probably firing 1,200 RPM from multiple barrels. maybe it's firing over 2000, modified to fire Cobalt projectiles. Did you ever wonder how loud it must be, down there? To hear that thing firing, for minutes on end? Days? Weeks? Months? You've lost a few runs by now, you're better. You're in your third week. The music shifts again. "APOCALYPSE ADVERTED" Displays a different message. Was it meant to be like this? It's going to be okay. By now, the enemy waves are relentless. Tough. You'll barely be scraping by - even with your management of nuclear warheads. if you have them at all. You accepted a long time ago that Quantity is far better to Quality, your nuclear warheads were downsized some time ago - a trade off you had to accept. You're making two per day, and it doesn't feel like enough. Four weeks in, or more. I was making four per day, downsized to the (relatively) small explosion size of most enemy projectiles. At this point, it's a glorified "Desperate Attempt to Parry enemy projectiles to set off a chain reaction." Four upgraded watch towers sit around my city, lighting up the skies above with laser fire and nuclear explosions from destroyed enemy munitions. An explosion grazes the top of the city. I lose a few million from the already dwindled population, I sit at about 16,000,000 from the original 70,000,000. Just a few days ago, a rift absorbed enough nuclear energy to spawn a bunch of space-anenome that ate tens of millions of citizens within seconds. It took me about 10 missiles back to back to clear that group in a panic. But the day is cleared. I see the upgrade screen, nothing left. Just citizens proposals. I write them off, as always. I laugh, seeing the last upgrade presented to me. I just want to tell you good luck, we're all counting on you. The music changed again. The game and I have an understanding. It was a long, arduous struggle. But Utopia Must Fall.

I'm in love with the tone of this game. Trying to fend off the apocalypse while the citizenry tries to come up with the dumbest ideas possible to deal with a situation that has a clear solution feels a lot like me buying UV resistant clothing while my phone is telling me its been near record temperatures outside every day for the past week. I'm the citizenry in this scenario. But Anyway. Utopia Must Fall is pretty tough, but in usual roguelite fashion once you get something going it becomes a lot of fun. There was a moment I had trying to fend off an onslaught of missiles and bombs for like 10 or 15 seconds with just my coil gun, one laser tower, two defense drones, and no shields, and we just barely made through it which felt awesome. The feeling of fighting for your life and then "Week 2" beats you over the head. It's so good. The visual presentation and sounds are putting in a ton of legwork obviously but they're not carrying the whole thing by any means. This is the second Pixeljam game Ive played and the second time Ive gone from not knowing if I liked the concept, to not being sure I liked the game, to thinking about the game while I'm trying to go to bed. It seems they know what theyre doing. And this one is still only in early access at the time of writing so thats exciting as well. Looking forward to more, and to seeing if the populace of Hyper Paris can bring me some better ideas to ignore in the future

The choices you have to make are trivial and the pool to pick from is so small one re-roll will give you the thing you wanted. There are so many things that could be added to make this a good game, but I would not pay the asking price for what you get right now.

The aesthetics are cool, but I don't particularly like the progression system. You are rewarded based on performance within a stage by meeting certain objectives. Play perfectly and you get bonus upgrades allowing you to scale your power faster, and thereby have a better chance of doing well the next stage. On the other hand, do poorly or get a couple suboptimal stages at the start and you fall immediately behind the curve, with no real shot of catching up. Later in the game the enemies turn into bullet sponges and it quickly becomes unfun. It's no longer enough to be mechanically good, you simply can't kill the enemies fast enough especially if you choose hermit mode (which gives a meager 10% points boost for massive downside). I'll give it some more time in the future, but right now I am tired of losing repeatedly on week 2 when the game decides to spawn multiple bullet sponge enemies simultaneously that all shoot homing missiles of certain doom. [Update] Played a bit more, made it to week 3. Still die most of time on week 2 when the enemy spawns overlap and shotgun my base simultaneously with multiple nukes. Pretty over the game in its current state of unfairness. Not worth 9 dollars when the runs all play out pretty much the same. Despite the upgrade availability being "randomized", you have a limited selection to pick from. Most are gated behind time delays, preventing you from going too far down specific paths. There are a number of upgrade nodes you pretty much have to take in order to survive.

I am mostly just leaving a positive review because I ultimately want this dev and this game to succeed. That being said, this game has some serious flaws and it seems like they may never be addressed at all. The GOOD: + There really isn't any game like this out there. It has a unique visual and play identity, and there just isn't anything else that scratches this particular itch in all of gaming. + The enemies are (mostly) unique and interesting to engage and work together in really satisfying ways. + The weapons are largely fun and unique and change the experience of play enough to justify their existence. + There is a chance we will get more regular weapons (and my fervent wish is that we also get more alternatives to nukes) and more game modes. The BAD: - The way this game handles difficulty is about the most uncreative and shortsighted I've ever seen. Every run ends exactly the same: You run out of upgrades and enemies (and projectiles) become far too spongy to stop and you watch helplessly as your city gets obliterated. This is not only boring (because each run can take over an hour) but it actively sabotages every other enjoyable aspect of the game. - This game is clearly balanced around the best players in the discord server, which means people who are not above average at this type of game will have no entry point and leave frustrated by the deliberately obtuse upgrade and difficulty system. The first week is so poorly thought out and balanced that you can restart 10 or 15 times in a row before you get the upgrades you want and an enemy pool that doesn't immediately create run ruining situations. Leaving your builds almost entirely to the mercy of RNG while kneecapping you for not playing optimally or choosing perfectly every single day. - Some builds are just better than others and require luck and optimal upgrade selection. There are 3 major upgrade paths in this game: Normal, Hermit and Berserker. Each have different week 1 requirements and are mostly just centered around whether you want to use nukes or not. On paper this sounds like a great way to add variety to a game that demands meticulous and tedious upgrade selection but in reality there is always a "meta" build that ends up being the obvious choice if you want to progress past a certain point in your scoring or days survived. You'll eventually find yourself playing the same way and making the same choices over and over again simply because you've seen all the upgrades and now all that's left is to beat your personal best. Where there should be experimentation, there is rote memorization and a tedious route to the top. - Nukes are the only real answer to bad luck or less than perfect play which leads to feeling like you have to hold on to as many as you can, and further chokes out trying new strategies against the game. - Limited opportunity upgrades are largely useless, uninteresting or just flat out do not change the gameplay enough to justify their existence. - Upgrades are random RNG with rerolls and you will reroll several times just to get even one of the upgrades you are looking for. And if you play well enough, you will have to waste a choice at least once on an upgrade you do not want yet. - The dev is stubbornly conservative about the end design of this game and will not take any risks (which, to be completely fair is their right as a solo dev) and this mentality is choking the life out of what could be one of the best games ever made. I also worry that the dev is only getting feedback from the best and most conservative players and this is creating an environment that stifles the potential of the game. - The scoring system is way too restrictive in the way it affects upgrades. You earn extra upgrades each day by completing certain kinds of scoring events (eliminating a squad before they can get in formation, killing a line of certain enemies in order etc.) but very quickly you need to get more and more of these scoring events to get a bonus upgrade. This ends up creating situations where you purposely play worse than you can or use valuable resources just to play the specific and singular way the game wants you to. And this also ends up stifling what upgrades you choose because most upgrades are gated by a specific day. You can get good, but the rush of overpowering the enemy with your armaments is always short lived and keeps you locked in the same cycles and playstyles. - The meta progression is just you unlocking what you used to have by default in previous versions of the game. It is not interesting and it is not satisfying and is clearly just there to waste some time in a game that already wastes your time liberally. I honestly have a lot more to say about this game, but I don't want to spend all day reviewing it so I'll leave with one final point: I used to really love this game and was excited for it's potential, but now I feel like I'm just watching it slowly suffocate because the dev either cannot take risks or is too afraid to.

As solid as many things are, this game lacks quite a bit in the way of how each game plays out. There are only 4 weapons with linear upgrades, and other damage upgrades are limited to (again) linear upgrade paths. A turret to shoot badies for you, that has a linear upgrade path, some drones that automatically attack targets, that have a linear upgrade path. It means that after just a handful of games you've seen everything the game has to offer. For a game nearly two years in the making, this feels like a game tossed together in half a year, or less, of work.

I was initially convinced I'd be hooked (it honestly hits so many great positives for me with the design style, graphics, theme, etc), but it's not balanced well in execution. I just find myself getting frustrated early against the exponential difficulty, and even more so if I make it further past a first or second boss. The game feels way too situational even if you figure out a strategy. I feel like some kind of meta progression where you can pick and choose upgrades to take into each game might help. Or, just make progression less punishing.

I adore this game, sank a lot of time into it and highly recommend to anyone but I despise how bad the health creep can ramp up. I'd rather be genuinely be beaten by the procedural waves than have the fun sucked out of the day 40+ waves because I have to focus fire enemies for up to 20+ seconds while managing a full screen of projectiles and I can't fire a nuke to help get some breathing space because of 2 alternating voids which are also incredibly tanky. I do love the challenge of the later days and I'm close to breaking 2 million points ( Can't wait for leader boards ) but the insane health most enemies get from about day 45+ really kills me on the inside at times and puts me off playing more because I know it's going to be an insane slog in the end game. Regardless this game is a blast, I love the direction it's went, the sound design, enemy design etc. Technosphere is my favourite part of the game, it's such a raw battle of endurance at times and the music gets me every time. I'm excited to see what's in store for the future and continue me and my friend's rivalry of one upping each other on our scores. This game will definitely end up as one of the games I put over 1000 hours into and I can't wait to see what happens in the meantime. Much love :^)

I bought this game because it was recommended by the Nova Drift dev and had a similar art style. The art style is great, but this dev could learn a lot from how Nova Drift handles difficulty and build diversity. My main problem with the game is how it scales difficulty. While later days introduce more complex enemies and send more enemies at once, enemy health increases rapidly. It seems to be the main form of difficulty scaling. Within the first week, even buying every weapon upgrade, an enemy wave that could be killed as they enter the screen requires two passes with the main weapon. It makes enemies feel very spongy and takes away from what is initially very crisp handling. I compare this to Nova drift where enemy health only starts to increase in the late game, and both enemy speed and damage are also used as scaling mechanics. Build diversity is also lacking. There are several different upgrade paths, and the game presents multiple choices with interesting trade offs. The problem I have found is that many of those paths seem like traps. The number of viable options is much lower than it first seems. I might just be bad at the game, but the bullet spongy enemies in particular do not motivate me to get better. I wish it had something like the artifact of glass from Risk of Rain; that would be much more fun. I hope that the early access period is used to improve some of these issues, and I will probably revisit the game on release. It has a great concept, style, and basic mechanics, but the execution needs work.

The most addictive game I've played in years. Insanely difficult after a certain point. For me that point came after killing the technosphere once after many failed attempts. I could only make it as far as level 40. I had to modify the code to give me hundreds of extra nukes to progress further unfortunately. After 100 hrs of play i've only made it to day 51 and at that point all the tree slections been filled for a long time and no new enemies will appear anyway. Further progression at that point requires me to give up shields for the city at the start and try to never take a single shot. Something that's pretty hard to accomplish without a major grind from day one. There really needs to be a multiple lives option or save states in the game to allow players to see all the enemies and experience the game fully. It's gets really crazy and fun after day 40 but at that point you had better have lots of spare nukes. Visually the game is stunning. Vector graphics will always hold a place in my heart because i grew up in the late 70's and all through the 80's in arcades. A vector game hasn't stunned me this much since I first started playing Tempest. There's nothing comparable to good vector graphic simulation and this is top tier. The audio is spectacular as well. An amazing sountrack and really satisfying sound effects. I can't praise this game enough. Hopefully there's further improvement and development of this and other games the devs have produced like Grid Ranger. More games on the horizon? Let's hope so.

This is an interesting game that scratches an itch of mine. It's a nice mix of elements from several games I've played before and I always enjoy a remix of all those good ol' games to see how different fun factors can come together to make something even more fun or intriguing. What's more, it can even play smoothly on a laptop with integrated graphics. I can't ask for more. If this is your first time playing this kind of game, one thing of note: Keep playing again and again. You're pretty much expected to get defeated and play again, unlock new bonuses along the way, and push your score ever higher. It's like old arcade games where you try to perfect your score, except that there's no hard score limit here. Don't stop. Keep trying! To devs: Thanks for making this! I hope to see something more "oomph". Maybe an AA flak cannon type of turret where the explosions occur on and around the cursor but doesn't hit anything in-between the turret and the cursor. Instant-hit but now you must trace the targets properly. I like flak cannons!

This game is really awesome, it has a fantastic asthetic with these little attention to details that makes it have such a great design like how we zoom out of the city we defend. I finally reached the second boss that had a health bar for the second time and I can certainly that it doesn't matter how good of a build you focus on, everything needs a buff except the scale of the foes. Don't get me wrong I LOVE a challenge, but when progression is tied to performing niche kill actions, then enemies don't need to escape before ever appearing in the first place. almost immediately by the 7th wave your primary weapon, support outposts, and hell even the nukes do almost nothing to help you get the perfect kill order or total wipe out of a squad before a single tiny minute mistake takes away what would have been nearly a very tiny bit more towards another "contract". I don't particularly love a single one of the primary weapon upgrades, the trash cannon is literally trash and should either be replaced or massively buffed, hell even the lovably comic telegraph pole launcher needs both damage and fire rate. the wave requirement to get more impact damage for every weapon should be reduced and more upgrades should more commonly add small amounts to this. finally dev I hope your reading this and don't think I'm trashing your game amigo, but we seriously need the small bonuses to either be much more rewarding or at least easier to pull off past wave 3. I tried going absolutely ham on the primary weapon and was constantly gate kept from the kind of damage needed for many of the bonuses, other times I would miss the very first target in the line and it would just barely pop into formation and then it became worthless to even bother continuing to focus that particular squad. other times I would massacre the beginning of a wave just to have the last 10 of them immediately break their flight path and escape before the next bullet of a 3600 rpm weapon even got to touch them. also like I mentioned earlier, some enemies just wouldn't even appear and have already escaped because I took out less than half their squad. mostly dev I would scale back on how fast the enemies gain HP, make them act slightly more consistently, still have them panic and fly crazily around screen when most of the squad was wiped. offer a few more chances and type of ways to get bonuses. Add a grace period to get bonuses (like for annhilation change it to wipe the squad before they get in formation AND fire the first round at you.) then just add slightly more damage to most of your damage sources, mostly just incrementally through most of the upgrades.
